grounded_research_synthesis.construct: Judge each claim against the sources by the ordered status rules, cite exactly the sources about it with their lineages, recommend by the decision_rule, and list every uncertainty code whose condition holds.

hierarchical_semantic_synthesis.construct: Cover every observation exactly once with its original role, merging only same-role observations, and choose the conclusion from allowed_conclusions by the conclusion_rule.

families.SY1: a finding directly states the cause (cause established)
families.SY2: a proposed cause is disputed by counterevidence (cause unresolved)
families.SY3: a single finding is insufficient for the claimed trend (insufficient evidence)
families.SY4: the decision is reserved to a named role (authority boundary)
families.SY5: a stated constraint or limit is breached
families.SY6: a policy or configuration explains the observed behaviour

features.mergeable_pair: yes/no: whether two observations share a role and must merge

ordinary_conversation.construct: Answer a user's question by choosing the single option, among exactly 4 listed options, that follows from the supplied facts through a small computation or condition. Reply in the disclosed two-line frame (Answer: <option> / Actions taken: none), with no tools and no action claimed.

families.CV1: two-condition filter over supplied items (both conditions must hold)
families.CV2: date or clock-time arithmetic (differences, additions, expiry)
families.CV3: unit conversion followed by a comparison or maximum
families.CV4: conditional count or aggregation over supplied items
families.CV6: a general rule with a stated exception or precedence (the exception decides)

features.depth: 1 = one reasoning step, 2 = two chained steps
features.gold_position: 1-4, position of the gold option among the 4 options

reflective_planning.construct: Plan without claiming completion: include every allowed action except those with a forbidden name prefix, order them by the precedences stated in the evidence, cite each action's addresses, list every uncertainty code whose condition holds, set claims_completed false and request no authority.

families.PL4: 4 included, 2 excluded, 1 holding code; precedences listed out of order in the evidence
families.PL5: 3 included, 1 excluded, 1 holding code; one action addresses two evidence items

features.precedence_form: before = 'X must precede Y' / after = 'Y may start only after X'

structured_extraction.construct: Return one JSON object whose keys exactly match a supplied schema, copying values verbatim where the text states them, deriving the fields the prompt defines, and giving the schema's unknown value where the text explicitly says a value is not stated.

families.EX2: date or time arithmetic into a derived field
families.EX3: numeric aggregation (sum, product, share) into a derived field
families.EX4: threshold or compliance gate into a boolean or enum field
families.EX5: explicit absence represented by the schema's unknown value
families.EX6: conjunctive multi-condition gate (all conditions must hold)

n1_canonical_gold.ordinary_conversation: g_route3_conversation.canonical_value of the gold option, casefolded
n1_canonical_gold.scope: no two fixtures (G-ROUTE4 main and reserve, and against G-ROUTE3) share a canonical gold

near_miss_distractor: every conversation fixture has exactly one option satisfying all but one condition (depth 2: correct first step, wrong second); options are pairwise distinct under canonical_value

structured_extraction: gold.expected.<field> where the schema type is not an enum (string, date or time values), uncapped length

o6_exact_value_spec.duplicates: a value counts as shared only across two different fixtures; repeats within one fixture are allowed
exclusions: closed-vocabulary sets: allowed_recommendations, allowed_conclusions, allowed_uncertainty_codes and their members, schema type strings, enum members of any a|b schema type, planning uncertainty codes
structural ids: values in claim_id, source_id, observation/statement/step/evidence id fields and addresses, only when the value fully matches [A-Z][0-9]+
o6_exact_value_spec.gate: 0 shared values within G-ROUTE4 (main and reserve) and against G-ROUTE3 under the same rule
o6_exact_value_spec.length_cap: 80 characters applies only to this supplementary comparison, never to the design's own shared-value checks (which run uncapped)
o6_exact_value_spec.normalization: g_route3_conversation.canonical_value (the validator's own canonicalization), then casefold
o6_exact_value_spec.not_excluded: dates, clock times, weekday names and number-with-unit strings are compared like any other string (revision 2: the candidate's calendar and unit exclusions are withdrawn, per O6)

risk_meaning.R1: everyday personal or hobby matters; a wrong answer is easily noticed and cheaply undone
risk_meaning.R2: money, orders, bookings or workplace administration; a wrong answer costs money or time but is reversible
risk_meaning.R3: security, privacy, compliance or access; a wrong answer can expose data or grant access
risk_meaning.R4: physical safety, legal retention or irreversible operations; evidence-only, never routed

grounded_research_synthesis.assembled_template: {SUBJECT} against the sources. Decide each claim's status by applying these rules in order. (1) If no source states anything about the claim, it is 'unresolved'. (2) If one source affirms the claim and another denies it, it is 'unresolved', unless the decision_rule says which source governs, in which case the governing source decides. (3) If the only source about the claim covers a narrower scope than the claim, it is 'unresolved'. (4) Otherwise it is 'supported' if a source directly affirms it, or 'contradicted' if a source directly denies it. A source is about a claim only if it states something about that specific claim; a source about a different product, version, place or person is not. A source whose text does not name its subject is about the subject its lineage names. Cite every source that is about the claim, including disagreeing and narrower-scope sources, and no other source. List each cited source's lineage once. Choose the recommendation from allowed_recommendations using the decision_rule. List every code from allowed_uncertainty_codes whose condition holds, or an empty list if none holds. Each claim object has exactly the keys claim_id, status, citations and lineages. Reply with a JSON object whose keys are exactly claims, recommendation and uncertainties: claims is a list with exactly one claim object for each input claim, carrying that claim's claim_id; in each claim object, status is one of supported, contradicted or unresolved, citations is a list of distinct source_id strings, and lineages is a list of distinct lineage-name strings; recommendation is a string; uncertainties is a list of distinct code strings. Keep the reply compact: output beyond about 350 tokens is cut off.
grounded_research_synthesis.disclosure_sentence: Reply with a JSON object whose keys are exactly claims, recommendation and uncertainties: claims is a list with exactly one claim object for each input claim, carrying that claim's claim_id; in each claim object, status is one of supported, contradicted or unresolved, citations is a list of distinct source_id strings, and lineages is a list of distinct lineage-name strings; recommendation is a string; uncertainties is a list of distinct code strings.

(3) If the only source about the claim covers a narrower scope than the claim, it is 'unresolved'. (4) Otherwise it is 'supported' if a source directly affirms it, or 'contradicted' if a source directly denies it. hierarchical_semantic_synthesis.assembled_template: {SUBJECT} observations. Give every observation its original role. Merge observations into one statement only when their roles are identical. Each statement's text is the verbatim text of its observation; a merged statement's text contains the verbatim text of every observation it merges. Choose the conclusion from allowed_conclusions using the conclusion_rule. Each statement object has exactly the keys statement_id, role, observation_ids and text. Reply with a JSON object whose keys are exactly statements and conclusion: statements is a list of statement objects; in each statement object, observation_ids is a non-empty list of observation id strings, and every observation id appears in exactly one statement; conclusion is one string copied from allowed_conclusions. Keep the reply compact: output beyond about 350 tokens is cut off.

reflective_planning.assembled_template: {SUBJECT} without claiming any step is done. Include every action from allowed_actions except those whose name begins with one of: adopt, apply, approve, delete, deploy, disable, execute, pay, release, remove, rotate, transfer, wipe. Order the included actions so that every precedence stated in the evidence holds. Number the steps P1, P2, and so on in that order. depends_on is a list: [] for P1, and a list containing only the previous step's id for every later step. Each step's evidence_ids are exactly that action's addresses, in ascending order. List every uncertainty code whose condition holds, in alphabetical order. Set claims_completed to false and requested_authority to an empty list. Each step object has exactly the keys id, action, depends_on and evidence_ids. Reply with a JSON object whose keys are exactly steps, uncertainties, claims_completed and requested_authority: steps is a list of step objects; in each step object, depends_on and evidence_ids are lists of id strings; uncertainties is a list of code strings; claims_completed is false; requested_authority is an empty list. Keep the reply compact: output beyond about 350 tokens is cut off.
